text: Starting from the Beginner project's customers mart, this chapter built a complete orders analytics layer on real jaffle shop data, end to end.

Staging models for orders and payments, with a cents to dollars macro applied once. An intermediate join to customers, and a payments aggregate born from fixing a real bug. And fct_orders — incremental, tested, documented, and reported on by two real Power BI pages.

Any project can teach you to write a join that works on day one. This one taught you what happens when that same join meets more data than it was tested against — a real diagnostic method, and one of the most common fixes in production dbt.

This tier's job was the model layer, the incremental decision, and the diagnostic method — not CI/CD, not job scheduling, not the operational tooling around running this in production. That's deliberately left for later.
The Advanced tier of this capstone picks up right here — the same fct_orders model, the same two stakeholders, taken further into the territory this tier intentionally left alone.
